findings: ACTOR SPOOFING (write-path audit integrity) — POST /api/staffing-desk/planner/apply persists a CLIENT-SUPPLIED actorId into every audit/author column. Controller src/modules/staffing-desk/presentation/staffing-desk.controller.ts:158-159 passes @Body() request straight to applyPlan without injecting req.principal. Service src/modules/staffing-desk/application/workforce-planner.service.ts:1514,1525,1562 forwards request.actorId into writeCanonicalDispatchPosition/writeCanonicalHirePositions, landing at ProjectPosition.createdByPersonId/updatedByPersonId (lines 1613-1614,1669-1671) and ProjectPositionFillHistory.changedByPersonId (lines 1626,1683). FE confirms it sends actorId in the body (frontend/src/lib/api/staffing-desk.ts:499-500,515-516). Any staffing-role user can attribute planner-applied positions and fill-history ledger rows to an arbitrary personId. The sibling create/transition/bulk-reassign endpoints correctly derive actorId from request.principal — this endpoint is the outlier.

ACTOR SPOOFING — POST /api/staffing-desk/planner/scenarios persists client-supplied dto.actorId into PlannerScenario.createdByPersonId. Controller src/modules/staffing-desk/presentation/staffing-desk.controller.ts:192-193 passes @Body() dto straight to create(); service src/modules/staffing-desk/application/planner-scenario.service.ts:119 writes dto.actorId to createdByPersonId. The PATCH/DELETE handlers on the same controller (lines 196-213) correctly source actorId from req.principal.personId, making the POST an inconsistent and exploitable outlier.

MISSING BODY VALIDATION — POST /staffing-desk/planner/apply, POST /staffing-desk/planner/scenarios, and POST /staffing-desk/team-builder (plus planner/extension-validate, planner/why-not, planner/auto-match) bind @Body() to TS INTERFACES (PlannerApplyRequestDto workforce-planner.service.ts:144; CreatePlannerScenarioDto planner-scenario.service.ts:28; TeamBuilderRequestDto team-builder.service.ts:12), not class-validator classes. The global ValidationPipe (src/main.ts:67-72, whitelist:true, forbidNonWhitelisted OFF) has no metatype to validate or whitelist-strip an interface, so these bodies are completely unvalidated — unchecked personId/projectId UUIDs, allocationPercent ranges, dates, and headcount flow straight into Prisma create/update calls. This is the validation-layer cause of the actor-spoofing findings above and also admits malformed write payloads.
evidence: Traced 7 in-scope POST endpoints (4 project-positions writes + planner/apply + planner/scenarios + team-builder). 4 project-positions write flows are SOUND: real awaited Prisma writes inside $transaction with fill-history ledger rows, class-validator DTOs (project-position-requests.ts), guards that fit, and actorId from request.principal. 2 staffing-desk write flows have a write-path actor-spoofing bug: planner/apply (controller staffing-desk.controller.ts:158-159 → service workforce-planner.service.ts:1514/1562/1613-1614/1626/1669-1671/1683) and planner/scenarios POST (controller :192-193 → service planner-scenario.service.ts:119) persist a CLIENT-SUPPLIED actorId into audit/author columns; FE sends it (frontend/src/lib/api/staffing-desk.ts:499-500,617-618). All staffing-desk POST bodies are interface-typed so the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:67-72) does not validate them. team-builder is read-only (no write).
